claim.value: Roster timing can shift apparent retention.
claim.scope: A possible influence on observed retention; its magnitude and direction are unspecified.

provenance.rationale: P026 explicitly identifies roster timing as a condition that can shift apparent retention.

signal_basis.value: Record intended roster dates and follow accounts through their next roster opportunity, observing waiting durations and publication timing. Publication near a previously stated roster date is a candidate timing signal.
signal_basis.scope: Prospective cohort observations with declared follow-up limits and censoring; the candidate signal is assumed observed for this assessment.

provenance.rationale: These spans supply roster-date collection, follow-up and censoring rules, retention measurements, and the candidate temporal alignment.
The bounded possibility claim is supported without an additional unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: Waiting duration and publication timing depend on when accounts resume progress. Their observed alignment with previously stated roster opportunities licenses treating roster timing as a possible influence on apparent retention. The claim does not identify a unique cause or assert a measured causal effect.
uncertainty: The influence's magnitude, direction, prevalence and causal contribution remain unspecified; other causes may produce similar timing.
